doc.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Current projects and discovering Joe Pesci as a jazz singer
summary: Jones runs through recent and planned collaborations (Snoop Dogg with Clark Terry, Stevie Wonder and Tony Bennett) and tells how Joe Pesci played him an album and surprised him with his jazz singing and pitch.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: . . . Ella, Sarah, Basie, Duke, Michael Jackson, Aretha, 50 Cent, Snoop Dogg. It’s ridiculous. I’m doing they album with Snoop Dogg and Clark Terry. That’s going to be great. They’re going to do mumbles. He’s going to rap bebop to hip-hop. I love that. Tony Bennett and Stevie – he asked me to do an album with him on Marvin Gaye songs – jazz. It’s great. Joe Pesci – one of the greatest jazz singers I ever heard in my life. Trust me. Eight years old. I used to hang out with him and Tommy Mottola and [Robert] DeNiro and him. We were just partying.

Uh-huh. No, no, no. The record guy. He was managing Hall and Oates back then. This was 17, 18 years ago. Just partying. Hanging out and stuff, and dogging it up. Just a few years ago, about two or three years ago, Joe asked me to come – because guys send me their records all the time. The actors, they love to sing. Jeff Bridges. All of them. River Phoenix. All of them, all the time. They want me – they’re into music, and they’re an affinity in them. But Joe said, “Q.” He was there with that little Jersey sound. He was behind the Jersey Boys too. Him and [Jack] Nicholson and all those guys – [John] Travolta. They’re all from Jersey. That’s the real gangsters, like Chicago. He says, “Q, I want you to hear my new album.” I said, “This is my only day off. I’ll listen to one. Okay, Joe?” He’s a beautiful cat. “Okay.” I could not believe what my ears heard. I suspected him to be what the guys were sending me before. Wrong. He’s got pitch like Sassy [Sarah Vaughan]. He’s got concert – because he’s a jazz singer. He’s been singing since he was eight years old. I could not believe it. I’m doing the album with him. I wrote the notes to an album after I heard it. He did it with Joey DeFrancesco, who can play.
Pat Martini [Martino], and the guy with John Clayton – Hamilton.
Killer, killer. Phrasing: Miles Davis phrasing, Lester phrasing. Everything. Pitch, feel, unbelievable. You’ll see. Adjectives don’t cover it.
